An Act to provide for the establishment of bonded
warehouses at places other than customs‑ports, and to afford facilities
for the bonding of salt in such warehouses
1. Title and construction.‑(1)
This Act may be called the Inland Bonded Warehouses Act, 1896.
(2) It shall be
read with, and taken as part of, the Sea Cus toms Act, 1878, VIII of 1878; (The word
"and" at the end of sub‑section (2) and sub‑section (3),
rep. by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1914 (10 of 1914), s. 3 and Sch. II.)*
(The
word "and" at the end of sub‑section (2) and sub‑section
(3), rep. by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1914 (10 of 1914), s. 3 and Sch.

Inland bonded warehouses and law applicable thereto

INLAND BONDED WAREHOUSES
4. Inland bonded warehouses and law applicable
thereto.‑(1) Notwithstanding anything
contained in the Sea Customs Act, 1878, the (Subs. by the Inland Bonded Warehouses
(Arndt.) Act, 1948, (11 of 1948), for "Chief Customs‑authority".)[Chief Customs‑Officer] may,
from time to time, (The words "with the previous sanction of the L. G."
rep. by the Inland Bonded Warehouses (Arndt.) Act, 1928 (4 of 1928), s. 2.)* * * appoint a public or license a
private ware house at any place which is not a warehousing port, and may (The words
"with the like sanction" rep. ibid.)* * * cancel such appointment or license VIII of 1878.
(The
proviso, which was ins. by s. 2, ibid., rep. by A. O., 1937.)* * * * * * *
(2) In reference
to such a place and a warehouse appointed or licensed thereat the provisions of
the said Act with respect to the levy of customs‑duties on goods brought
in bond from one cus toms‑port to another, and with respect to
warehousing, shall be construed as if the place were a customs‑port and a
warehousing port, and the warehouse a public or a private warehouse, as the
case may be, appointed or licensed thereat under that Act (Ins. by Act 4 of 1928, s. 2.) [and, if the owner so desires, as if
goods, in respect of which the pro cedure laid down in sections 90, 91 and 92
of the said Act has been complied with, were goods already warehoused at a ware housing
port within the meaning of section 105 of the said Act].
(3) All rules
applicable to such warehouses, and to the weigh ment and removal thereto of
salt, and in force at the commence ment of this Act, shall remain so applicable
until they shall be duly superseded or altered.
(Sub‑section
(4) rep. by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1914 (10 of 1914), s. 3 and Sch.
II.)* * * * *

Conveyance of salt to inland bonded warehouses under bound

THE INLAND BONDED WAREHOUSES ACT, 1896
|THE INLAND BONDED WAREHOUSES ACT, 1896
ACT No. VIII OF 1896
[5th
March, 1896]
An Act to provide for the establishment of bonded
warehouses at places other than customs‑ports, and to afford facilities
for the bonding of salt in such warehouses
SALT TIME‑BONDS
5. Conveyance of salt to inland bonded warehouses
under bound. Notwithstanding anything contained in
the Sea Customs Act, 1878, or in section 4 of this Act, the (Subs. by the
Inland Bonded Warehouses (Arndt.) Act, 1948, (11 of 1948), for "Chief
Customs‑authority".)
[Chief Customs‑Officer] may permit salt removed from ship board or from a
warehouse appointed or licensed under the Sea Customs Act, 1878, to be
conveyed, under a bond securing the subsequent payment of the duty leviable in
respect of the salt so removed and in accordance with such rules as may be
prescribed in this behalf by the (Subs. by Act 4 of 1928, s. 3, for "L. G.") [Chief Customs‑authority], to a
warehouse appointed or licensed for that purpose by the (Subs. by the Inland Bonded Warehouses
(Amdt.) Act, 1948 (11 of 1948), for "Chief Customs‑authority".)[Chief Customs‑Officer].

Form of bound

6. Form of bound. Every
bond executed in accordance with the provisions of the last preceding section
shall be in the form hereto annexed, or, when such form is inapplicable or
insufficient, in such other form as is from time to time prescribed by the
Chief Customs‑authority:
Provided that
the time allowed by such bond for the payment of the duty leviable on the salt
included therein shall not exceed the time within which it may reasonably be
expected that the whole of such salt shall have passed into consumption, and
shall in no case exceed six months:
Provided, also,
that the (Subs.
by the Inland Bonded Warehouses (Amdt.) Act, 1948 (11 of 1948), for "Chief
Customs‑authority".)
[Chief Customs‑Officer] may at any time require the duty to be paid to
the extent to which the salt may have been delivered from the warehouse.

7. Power to makes rules.
The (Subs.
by the Inland Bonded Warehouses (Amdt.) Act, 1928 (4 of 1928), s. 3, for
"L. G.") [Chief
Customs‑authority] may (The words "with the previous sanction of the G.G. in
C." rep. by the Decentralization Act, 1914 (4 of 1914), s. 2 and Sch., Pt.
1.)* * * make rules(For rules made
by the Government of Bengal under this section, see Den. R. & O. (Form of
Bond)), consistent with the
provisions of this Act, to regulate‑
(1) the
appointment or licensing of warehouses under section 5;
(2) the
inspection by Government officers of such ware houses;
(3) the safe
custody of salt in transit under the provisions of the said section;
(4) the removal
of salt from a warehouse appointed or licensed under the said section;
(5) the nature
of the security to be required from a person executing a bond in accordance
with the provisions of the said section and the time and place of payment of
'the sum recoverable under such bond; and
(6) generally such other matters as may be
deemed neces sary to secure the safety of the public revenue.
